processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heating ramp of the Gleeble-3500 hot-compression schedule prior to homogenization.
Cooling from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 1050 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held 15 s so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was uniform.

Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression at 1050 °C and 0.1 s^-1 applied with a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were placed on both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
Immediately after compression the sample was water-spray quenched.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (as-forged billet) microstructure: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous etched boundaries with dark grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced parallel light striations (segregation/dendritic banding); chemically heterogeneous, no uniform solid solution.

phases_present.morphology: large polygonal grains; dark grain interiors with fine parallel light striations varying in direction from grain to grain

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length.

structures.overall_structure: Post-hot-deformation structure: dynamic recrystallization (DRX) whose degree increases with temperature and with decreasing strain rate and whose degree is greatest in the large-deformation zone (zone 3) and least in the difficult-deformation zone (zone 1); the DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature. The paper does not present a dedicated micrograph for 1050 °C/0.1 s^-1.

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (zone 3, core of compressed specimen)

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed dynamically recrystallized grains growing with temperature; at 1050 °C DRX is basically completed within the large deformation zone

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; measured from the core (large deformation zone) of the compressed sample.

measurement_conditions.environment: isothermal constant-strain-rate compression; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant between the specimen and pressure heads
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical specimen F 8 mm × 12 mm with perpendicular end faces
measurement_conditions.test_standard: Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator, isothermal constant strain rate compression to 60% (true strain 0.92)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: True stress–true strain compression curve; all curves rise to a peak then soften to a plateau (Fig. 3). No numeric flow-stress value is reported specifically for 1050 °C/0.1 s^-1.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Rheological/flow stress curve of Fe-Mn-Al-C steel for the deformation condition (dataset part of the T/ε̇ family in Fig. 3); rises to a peak (peak strain about 0.1-0.2) then softens to a plateau.

characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing (thermo-mechanical simulation)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900-1150 °C; strain rates 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 s^-1; max compression 60% (true strain 0.92); specimen F 8 mm × 12 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire rheological (flow) stress curves to analyze hot deformation and DRX behavior.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; flow stress decreases with increasing T or decreasing strain rate. At 0.01 s^-1 peak stress falls from 305.4 MPa (900 °C) to 53.8 MPa (1150 °C), and at 10 s^-1 it falls 73% over the same range.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: After compression the sample was split in half along the axial axis, prepared by grinding, polishing and etching.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe microstructure evolution in the three deformation zones and measure DRX average grain size.
characterization_methods.key_findings: DRX degree: zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation); with increasing T the DRX volume fraction increases.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etching solution: 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)

computational_details.simulation_method: constitutive analysis by the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine function and the Zener-Hollomon (Z) parameter
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Peak stress σp at T = 900-1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.01-10 s^-1; R = 8.314 J/(mol·K); 1000/T scaling.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The fitted straight lines in Fig. 4 are not parallel, so the calculated activation energy is only the average value within the experimental range; the Z parameter trends match those of the flow stress and the phenomena are reported as reproducible.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate peak stress, temperature and strain rate to determine the DRX activation energy Qp.

parameters.name: k1 (average slope, ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)])

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain rate that characterizes the combined influence of T and ε̇ on flow stress and normalizes the flow-curve characteristic values.
analytical_models.model_note: Table 1 tabulates lnZ for all T and ε̇; for this sample's condition (1050 °C, 0.1 s^-1) lnZ = 58.60.

analytical_models.model_name: Cingara-McQueen equation and derived critical strain relation
analytical_models.equation_role: Determine the critical strain/stress (εc/σc) for onset of DRX via the inflection point of the work-hardening-rate curve.
analytical_models.model_note: The C value shown in Fig. 5 is C = 0.1461 (R = 0.9728) at 1050 °C, 0.01 s^-1 — a different strain rate from this sample; C values for other T and ε̇ were also obtained.

analytical_models.model_name: Flow-curve characteristic value models as functions of lnZ (eq. 10)
analytical_models.equation_role: Multiple-linear-regression models linking the critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress of DRX to the Zener-Hollomon parameter.
analytical_models.model_note: The DRX state diagram (Fig. 7) derived from these models defines area A (work hardening), area B (partial DRX) and area C (complete DRX); εc and εs increase with lnZ.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (eq. 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict the DRX average grain size for numerical simulation of hot forming.
analytical_models.model_note: Model obtained by Levenberg-Marquardt regression; correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% for all samples, with absolute error mostly within 3 µm.

computational_details.simulation_method: finite element simulation of hot compression
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid plastic body; die indenter set as a rigid body with material parameters; semi-symmetric specimen used as the deformation model; contact interface friction set to shear type with value 0.3; billet-air convection coefficient 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulation was in line with the experimental conditions of thermal compression.

unmapped_findings: For the sample condition 1050 °C/0.1 s^-1 the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 58.60 (Table 1).
The material is a Fe-Mn-Al-C steel of a single forging-billet heat with composition (mass fraction, %) 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb, balance Fe (b0018).

The paper's recommended window for obtaining a fine and uniform grain structure is 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 and 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1; the present condition (1050 °C/0.1 s^-1) lies outside both windows, so it is not identified as giving a fine uniform DRX structure (b0012, b0065, b0086).

DRX behavior: the steel is negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive; peak stress decreases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 0.01 s^-1 peak stress falls from 305.4 MPa (900 °C) to 53.8 MPa (1150 °C) (82% reduction) and at 10 s^-1 it falls 73% over the same range (b0024).
The DRX activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (b0032).
DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 the grain size exceeds 70 µm (coarse-grain structure) (b0063, figure_010).
The material was confirmed to show reproducibility of the reported experimental phenomena under identical experimental conditions for the same steel batch/composition (b0018, b0012).
